clinician.trajectory_summary: An adolescent female presented with a 4-year history of gradually enlarging, painless swelling over the left upper back in the scapular region. Physical examination revealed a 12×11 cm firm, non-tender, smooth-surfaced, immobile mass over the left scapular region extending from 6 cm below the head of humerus superiorly to the seventh intercostal space inferiorly, with normal distal pulses and neurological examination. Plain radiography of the chest was normal. MRI of the left scapula demonstrated a hyperintense lesion (12×1.7×12 cm) in the left paravertebral region extending from D5 to D12, which was suppressed on STIR sequence, consistent with lipoma. Tru-cut biopsy was performed and was suggestive of lipoma. The patient subsequently underwent surgical excision, and histopathology of the excised specimen confirmed the diagnosis of lipoma.
